challenge.name: The Missing Gate
challenge.description: A critical compliance audit has revealed that our model promotion process lacks a formal quality gate. #requirements_reuben# insists that acceptance criteria must be fully automated and governed to meet security standards, and he will not compromise on this. #automation_alex# argues that the current manual checks are sufficient for now and that building an automated gate will delay the release of new features.
challenge.roundIntroduction: The compliance team has flagged a gap in our production pipeline where models are deployed without verified acceptance criteria. This has left the team scrambling to decide how to handle the validation step immediately.

on_enter_ops.reason: The compliance audit found no defined criteria for model approval

stalemate_ops.reason: Uncertainty over acceptance criteria has frozen the business metric definitions

roster.name: Efficiency Emilia
roster.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.
roster.priorities: Applying deep domain knowledge to ensure models fulfill specific business goals. Aligning ML solutions with clear objectives, KPIs, and business goals. Making organization-level decisions and enhancing overall operational capability. Defining products by defining and optimizing product features.

roster.name: Requirements Reuben
roster.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.
roster.priorities: Guaranteeing high product quality through rigorous testing of applications. Guaranteeing the integrity, confidentiality, and security of all ML assets. Meeting internal and external compliance and data protection standards. Keeping infrastructure stable, reproducible, and cost-controlled.

roster.name: Automation Alex
roster.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.
roster.priorities: Building automated pipelines and maintaining full system operational stability. Ensuring seamless deployment, integration, and stability of models and services in production.

roster.name: Reliability Ruth
roster.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.
roster.priorities: Pushes the delivery of reliable ML-powered features that directly improve the user experience. CI/CD and working feedback loops. Identifying and reporting issues to facilitate iterative improvements.

items.fact: {requirements_reuben} proposed that the acceptance criteria process must be governed to meet security standards.

readings.driver: He wants the acceptance criteria to be fully governed to ensure every model meets the security bar.
readings.boundary: He will not approve any model promotion unless the acceptance criteria are governed.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a manual process if it meant faster feature releases.
readings.fact: That is simply how the acceptance criteria setup works today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} asked for the acceptance criteria to remain manual to avoid delaying new features.

readings.driver: He wants to keep the acceptance criteria manual so that new features can be released without delay.
readings.boundary: He will not accept any change to the acceptance criteria process.
readings.trade_off: He would give up manual checks if the release schedule is tight.
readings.fact: That is simply how the acceptance criteria setup works today.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} suggested defining KPIs to align model performance with business goals.

readings.driver: She wants the KPI definitions to be automated so that business goals are tracked consistently.
readings.boundary: She will not proceed without clear KPI definitions.
readings.trade_off: She would accept missing KPIs if it meant faster model deployment.
readings.fact: That is simply how the KPI definition setup works today.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} mentioned that the lack of a quality gate makes it hard to monitor model performance in production.

readings.driver: She wants the acceptance criteria to be automated to improve production monitoring.
readings.boundary: She will not deploy models without a quality gate.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a manual gate if it meant faster deployment of user facing features.
readings.fact: That is simply how the acceptance criteria setup works today.

items.fact: {efficiency_emilia} noted that the cost of building a governed gate impacts the operational budget.

readings.driver: She wants to optimize costs by automating the gate efficiently.
readings.boundary: She will not approve spending beyond the current operational budget.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a higher cost for the gate if it ensures long term efficiency gains.
readings.fact: That is simply how the budget allocation works today.

items.fact: {automation_alex} suggested that the pipeline needs a stable trigger to handle acceptance checks.

readings.driver: He wants the trigger to be automated so that the pipeline runs reliably without manual intervention.
readings.boundary: He will not change the trigger if it risks breaking the deployment schedule.
readings.trade_off: He would accept a manual trigger if it meant less complexity in the pipeline.
readings.fact: That is simply how the pipeline trigger works today.

items.fact: {reliability_ruth} proposed that the risk assessment must feed into the acceptance criteria to catch issues early.

readings.driver: She wants the link to be governed so that feedback loops are tight.
readings.boundary: She will not release models if the risk assessment does not inform the acceptance criteria.
readings.trade_off: She would accept a loose link if it meant faster time to market.
readings.fact: That is simply how the link works today.

readings.driver: Someone wants the KPI definitions to be automated to track business goals.
readings.boundary: A stakeholder will not proceed without KPI definitions.
readings.trade_off: A stakeholder would accept missing KPI definitions for faster deployment.
readings.fact: That is simply how the KPI definition setup works today.

items.fact: The acceptance criteria process is broken.

readings.driver: Someone wants the acceptance criteria to be automated to meet security standards.
readings.boundary: A stakeholder will not approve models without governed acceptance criteria.
readings.trade_off: A stakeholder would accept a broken process if it meant faster releases.
readings.fact: That is simply how the acceptance criteria setup works today.

items.fact: The data contracts are managed manually.

readings.driver: Someone wants the data contracts to be automated to ensure data quality.
readings.boundary: A stakeholder will not accept manual data contracts for production models.
readings.trade_off: A stakeholder would accept manual data contracts if it meant faster data ingestion.
readings.fact: That is simply how the data contracts setup works today.

items.fact: The risk assessment is conducted manually.

readings.driver: Someone wants the risk assessment to be automated to catch risks faster.
readings.boundary: A stakeholder will not accept manual risk assessments for compliance.
readings.trade_off: A stakeholder would accept manual risk assessments if it meant faster model approval.
readings.fact: That is simply how the risk assessment setup works today.

items.fact: The link from risk assessment to acceptance criteria has no trigger.

readings.driver: Someone wants the link from risk assessment to acceptance criteria to be automated.
readings.boundary: A stakeholder will not accept a link without a trigger for compliance.
readings.trade_off: A stakeholder would accept a link without a trigger if it meant faster acceptance criteria updates.
readings.fact: That is simply how the link from risk assessment to acceptance criteria works today.
